hook.text: You haven't updated your LinkedIn in two years. Your last blog post was in 2022. Your brand is decaying.

buildup.text: Like technical debt, brand debt accumulates when you stop investing in your professional presence.

discovery.text: Stale profiles signal disengagement. Outdated content misrepresents your current capabilities.

twist.text: Brand debt compounds. The longer you wait, the bigger the gap between perception and reality.

climax.text: Schedule quarterly brand maintenance: update profiles, publish one piece, and refresh your story.

punchline.text: A brand unused is a brand you'll have to rebuild.

quiz.question: What is personal brand debt?
options: Accumulated decay from not investing in your professional presence

details.summary: Personal brand debt accumulates when you neglect your professional presence, let your online profiles go stale, or allow your reputation to diverge from your current capabilities. Like technical debt, it compounds over time and becomes increasingly expensive to repay.
details.whyItMatters: Brand debt means missed opportunities are invisible to you. An outdated profile or stale portfolio silently disqualifies you from opportunities before you even learn they existed.
takeaways: Stale profiles and outdated skills descriptions create brand debt
Schedule quarterly brand maintenance to prevent accumulation
Paying down brand debt requires concentrated visible effort

faq.question: What are the biggest sources of personal brand debt?
faq.answer: An outdated LinkedIn profile, inactive professional social media accounts, a stale portfolio, and allowing others to define your reputation through inaction. Each month of neglect adds debt that requires progressively more effort to correct.

faq.question: How do you pay down accumulated personal brand debt quickly?
faq.answer: Update all online profiles in one focused session, publish two to three pieces of content in your first week, and reach out to ten dormant professional contacts. This intensive sprint reactivates your presence. Then establish quarterly maintenance to prevent re-accumulation.
